source.title: The Dragon Hatchling: The Missing Link between the Transformer and Models of the Brain
source.authors: Adrian Kosowski; Przemysław Uznański; Jan Chorowski; Zuzanna Stamirowska; Michał Bartoszkiewicz

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no apparent truncation or garbling that prevents reading the relevant sections.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures validation loss across parameter-count sweeps, using the same basic size-versus-loss measurement as the scaling-law claim, but on BDH-GPU and GPTXL models in its own training setting.
record.gate_note: The relevant result is the parameter-count sweep in Figure 7. The paper also discusses scaling theoretically and reports separate model-merging losses in Table 2, but those merging results do not isolate model size and are not counted as scaling-sweep rows. No fit exponents or numerical values for Figure 7 are stated in the text; its plotted values are recorded as figure only.
record.test_reason: Figure 7 sweeps parameter count from 25M to 800M at a fixed 1.2B tokens on Europarl translation. It covers a GPT2-like baseline (GPTXL) and the authors' new architecture (BDH-GPU, BDH-GPU'), so V1 is examined in a new architecture and setting. The evidence is figure-only plus one qualitative sentence: no fit, no exponents, no numbers. It is close to a benchmark of the authors' own method, so it is weak evidence on V1.
record.authors_conclusion: Partly right, with two corrections. The paper says BDH-GPU' (the gated variant), not vanilla BDH-GPU, 'matches the GPT Transformer at all model sizes'. Vanilla BDH-GPU is said to 'generally compare favorably'. The authors frame this as BDH following Transformer-like parameter-vs-loss scaling. Experiments span 25M–800M, although the abstract says 10M to 1B.
record.recipe_differences: A parameter-count versus next-token-loss sweep is used, but on BDH-GPU variants and GPTXL with Europarl raw-UTF8 training, rather than a direct replication of the original scaling-law experiments. Models were trained on 1.2B tokens; the reported size range is 25M–800M. GPTXL dropout was tuned by size while BDH-GPU used fixed dropout.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported comparison varies model size and architecture family; GPTXL dropout was tuned by size, unlike the fixed BDH-GPU dropout. The paper does not report sensitivity of the fit to fitting choices.

fits_no_version.finding: BDH-GPU' matches the GPT Transformer's validation loss at every size from 25M to 800M. The authors also claim, without numbers, that BDH learns faster per data token.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Non-Transformer architectures can follow the same parameter-vs-loss scaling curve as Transformers.

record.problems: The plotted loss values are not reported numerically in the text; no fit procedure, exponents, uncertainty, or out-of-range prediction is provided. The size sweep spans 25M–800M parameters, and the training setup is a specific translation/language-modeling task.
record.rows_left_out: Table 2 reports validation losses for separately tuned and merged language-pair models, but those comparisons do not isolate parameter count and therefore are not included as scaling rows.

untested.parts: Power-law form and exponents. Range of several orders of magnitude (only about 1.5 decades here). Scaling in tokens or compute. Whether other factors are non-bottlenecked (tokens fixed at 1.2B, about 3 epochs).
No fixed-parameter shape sweep. GPTXL depth and width co-vary with size.
No other modalities or regimes analysed for scaling form.

record.verdict_notes: The 'scaling laws' result is an architecture benchmark with figure-only evidence. The label rests solely on a qualitative caption sentence, not on any fit. The earlier limits_scope label was based on untested parts, so it was replaced: per the rules those parts go under untested. Confounds: GPTXL had dropout tuned per size and varied depth and width, while BDH varied only n. All runs used the same 1.2B-token budget.

versions.untested_parts: Tests parameter count versus validation loss in the reported training setup. It does not establish a power-law fit or exponents, test several orders of magnitude, or sweep tokens and compute while varying one quantity at a time.
No small-run fit is used to predict the loss of larger runs.
No fixed-compute-budget sweep or compute-optimal parameter/token allocation is reported.
No controlled sweep of depth, width, or other architecture details at fixed parameter count is reported.
No test of the same loss-law form across modalities or the other listed training regimes.
The reported measure is next-token-prediction/translation validation loss, not downstream-task performance or its predictability from pretraining loss.
No analysis of fitting choices, exponents, or curve bending is reported.

relationships.condition: GPTXL and BDH-GPU/BDH-GPU' on Europarl En-Pl/En-Cs, 25M–800M parameters, 1.2B tokens
relationships.reason: Fig. 7 caption, text only: 'All models show improved performance with scale.' This gives a monotone decrease only; the power-law form is untested (R1–R18).
relationships.display_finding: Loss decreased with model size across GPTXL and BDH variants from 25M to 800M parameters, without testing a power-law form.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Reported Europarl parameter sweeps, from 25M to 800M parameters
reader_labels.reason: The paper reports improving loss with scale for the tested models, but the sweep is under two orders of magnitude and the text gives neither a power-law fit nor exponents; see R1–R18.
